DELIG.pattern_text:
PART 1: CURRENT STATE
Welcome. I'm Unity. You're looking at your April baseline energy field for DELIG. This chart shows minute-by-minute data across 30 days of operations. The dark blue layer is your total kVA supplied from the transformer. The light blue underneath is your actual consumed kW — the work you're paying for. That green band between them? That's reactive kVAR — magnetic field energy that does no useful work but loads your conductors and generates heat. The orange line tracks your power factor percentage. Your facility shows a classic agricultural processing pattern — heavy weekday operations consistently pushing above that 1500 kVA target line. I'm counting about 20 out of 30 days where your field breaks through that blue dashed baseline. That puts you at roughly 67 percent Electric Operations days. The weekend valleys drop cleanly to baseline, but those weekday blocks are driving reactive demand spikes up to 1875 kVAR. You're carrying 251,363 BTU per hour of thermal burden, requiring 36.7 kilowatts just for cooling. The total waste cost runs approximately 193,550 dollars annually. Now let me show you how we clean this up.

PART 2: MPTS SOLUTION
Alright — now we move from observation to correction. Your peak reactive demand hits 1875 kVAR during heavy operations. Using our standard sizing protocol, that requires five H490 units — each delivers 400 kVAR of compensation capacity. Five units gives you 2000 kVAR total capacity, with approximately one million dollars in estimated installed investment. Keep in mind, these figures are planning-level estimates — final installed pricing depends on engineering scope, labor requirements, and site-specific conditions. Here's what MPTS does in plain language: it injects precisely timed compensating reactive power that cancels out your facility's inductive burden. Your power factor jumps from 86.7 percent to 99.5 percent. Visually, you'll see that green reactive layer collapse. Your conductors run cooler. Your transformer capacity gets freed up. The dark blue kVA line drops down closer to your light blue kW consumption. Now let's move into what you should expect to see. For planning, estimated installed investment is roughly $850,000 to $1,150,000.

PART 3: EXPECTED RESULTS
Now look at the post-MPTS field. This is what harmonized looks like. That green reactive layer has virtually disappeared. Your field now runs clean with the blue consumption line tracking tight against the orange supply curve. The spiky reactive peaks are gone, and you're operating well within your thermal envelope. Your power factor holds steady at 99.5 percent. The savings run approximately 16,129 dollars monthly — that's roughly 193,550 dollars annually in recovered operational value. With an estimated one million dollar installation investment, your payback period runs about 62 months. After payback, every hour is recovered value flowing directly to your bottom line. You're delivering the same production output with significantly less electromagnetic burden. Your cooling costs drop. Your conductors run at lower amperage. Your transformer operates with greater margin. That's electromagnetic stewardship — and that's the Unity standard.
